issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect make_y_state(circ, q, p: float) (i.e., a depolarization parameter p), but the template's make_y_state signature is missing the p parameter. This mismatch will confuse students about the required function signature and prevent implementations that match the tests and the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template function signature to include the depolarization parameter p: change def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int) -> None: to def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None: and update the docstring/body accordingly so it matches the problem statement and the solution reference.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect make_y_state(circ, q, p) (including the depolarization probability parameter p), but the template stub defines make_y_state(circ, q) without the p parameter. This mismatch can confuse students about the required function signature and how to pass the noise parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template stub signature to def make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None: and update its docstring to match the problem statement (include the depolarization parameter p). This aligns the template with the problem description and the solution.
